thread:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — nightly CI shows a P99 token latency +22% after yesterday's runtime change that moves kernel selection earlier in the request pipeline. Uploading traces now.

Maya Chen: nsys: s3://redwood-traces/2234/nsys_warmup_2234.qdrep (nvtx + kernels). Perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/2234-warmup

perf-bot: regression alert detected: p99 +22% (baseline vs nightly), affected route: /v1/generate, sample size 3000 requests.

Jun Park: Can you paste a short diff or commit hash?

Maya Chen: commit: 6f3a9c2 — change: pick_kernel_async moved to pre-batch stage and reduced coalescing window to 4ms.

Alex R.: Quick skim of nsys: I see a lot more small kernel launches and repeated memcpy calls in the first ~200 tokens. Looks like fused-gemm variant isn't being chosen, fallback to smaller kernels.

Alex R.: nvprof-ish excerpt (from nsys summary):
```
KernelName           Calls   AvgTime(us)   TotalTime(ms)
fused_gemm           18      1.2e3         21.6
gemm_small            140     120           16.8
memcpy_h2d            98      55            5.4
```

Priya S.: Hmm — that aligns with a kernel-selection heuristic regression. Moving selection earlier could be losing sequence-length context used by the selector, so it picks narrower kernels to be safe. Also coalescing window reduction prevents grouping of short requests into a fused path.

Jun Park: I ran a controlled compare on a synthetic 128-token workload:
- old selector: P99=98ms, avg=45ms
- new selector: P99=119ms, avg=48ms
So tail is impacted, avg not much.

Maya Chen: Also noticed KV-cache miss rate for prefix keys jumped from 2%->9% during warmup in the perf trace. That explains memcpy chatter — cache population is less efficient.

Alex R.: Repro steps I used:
```
# run nsys capture for deterministic workload
RUNTIME_TRACE=1 RUNTIME_KERNEL_SELECTOR=experimental nsys profile -o /tmp/run.qdrep -- python3 -m tests.microbench --seq-len 128 --batch 1 --repeat 1000
```

Priya S.: Good. Can someone bisect to the commit boundary? If 6f3a9c2 is the first bad commit we should confirm the smallest change that regressed behavior.

Jun Park: I started a git bisect yesterday morning and narrowed to two candidates: 6f3a9c2 and 72d1b0f. 72d1b0f is a follow-up micro-optimization to scheduling. Reverting 6f3a9c2 locally restores fused_gemm selection and P99 drops back ~20%.

ci-bot: CI build for revert-6f3a9c2: https://ci.redwood/2234/build/512 — tests passed (perf-run flagged unstable).

Maya Chen: What's the root cause theory? My take: moving selector earlier means it doesn't see batched request aggregation info (the coalescer was downstream), so it picks conservative kernels per-request. The reduced coalescing window further limits grouping, producing many small launches and KV warmup thrash.

Alex R.: Agreed. Also saw scheduler traces showing more preemption events for short kernels — that increases observed latency variance. Perfetto timeline shows frequent kernel gaps of ~30-80us where GPU sits idle between tiny launches.

Jun Park: Patch idea: keep kernel selection at post-coalesce stage OR propagate coalescer hints to the selector (a cheap bitset that says "likely to be fused"). Also revert coalescing window reduction from 4ms->8ms for warmup.

Priya S.: I'd prefer the hint approach so we don't lose the intended async early selection benefit for long-running requests. Patch plan: 1) add coalesce_hint flag to request meta; 2) selector reads flag and prefers fused variants when set; 3) tests to ensure for first N tokens we prefer fused kernels.

Maya Chen: Can someone run a microbench with hints toggled? I can run nightly perf after the change.

Alex R.: I pushed a small branch: feature/selector-hints. Local run: P99 improved from 119ms->101ms (still slightly higher than baseline but much better). Uploading trace: s3://redwood-traces/2234/selector-hints.qdrep

perf-bot: quick compare summary:
- baseline (pre-6f3a9c2): p99=98ms, avg=45ms
- nightly (post-6f3a9c2): p99=119ms, avg=48ms
- selector-hints branch: p99=101ms, avg=46ms

Jun Park: That's promising. Next: run against real traffic for an hour on staging and watch KV miss rates + memcpy hotspots.

Priya S.: I'll add unit tests for coalescer->selector metadata and an e2e perf harness entry in ci that exercises warmup for 2k requests.

Maya Chen: Assigning follow-ups: @Alex R. validate hint flag under load; @Priya S. add tests and rollout guard; @Jun Park continue bisect logs and confirm smallest revertable change. I'll coordinate staging perf runs and update the incident doc. :thumbsup:

Alex R.: done, starting load job now, will post results here.

Jun Park: saving traces and bisect notes to the internal perf folder: internal/perf/regressions/2026-03-17-kernel-selector-warmup.md

Maya Chen: Thanks team. If the hint patch stabilizes P99 in staging we'll ship revert+hint as a short-lived fix and iterate on selector placement properly.

Alex R.: quick note — if we can't converge fast, we should gate the early-selector behind a feature flag per-deployment to avoid global rollout.

Priya S.: Agreed. I'll add the feature flag in the rollout policy.

Maya Chen: closing loop after staging runs. Will post final perf diff and timeline snippets.
